title: Composing finiteness and surgery for rational PD groups
question: Rational Poincar\'e duality groups are often said to behave like fundamental groups of closed manifolds. Suppose \Gamma is such a group in dimension n, \omega(\Gamma)\in\\widetilde K_0(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]) vanishes, and the 2-torsion lattice hypotheses guarantee the relevant L-group assembly map is zero. How do these ingredients combine to produce an actual closed n-manifold with \pi_1=\Gamma? In particular, how do we pass from the algebraic PD condition to an FH(\mathbb Q) complex, then to a degree-one normal map, and finally through Wall's surgery exact sequence to eliminate the obstruction class?
answer:
Start with the finiteness obstruction. A finitely presented PD_n^{\mathbb Q} group \Gamma has a classifying space B\Gamma whose universal cover is \mathbb Q-acyclic. Wall's obstruction \omega(\Gamma)\in\widetilde K_0(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]) measures whether this \mathbb Z[\Gamma]-complex is chain-homotopy equivalent to a finite complex. The assumption \omega(\Gamma)=0 lets us replace B\Gamma by a finite CW complex X with \pi_1(X)=\Gamma. Because \Gamma is PD_n^{\mathbb Q}, cap product with the fundamental class in H_n(X;\mathbb Q) furnishes isomorphisms H^i(X;\mathbb Q)\cong H_{n-i}(X;\mathbb Q), so X is a rational Poincar'e (FH(\mathbb Q)) complex.

Next we build a geometric representative. Take the n-skeleton of X, attach handles to obtain an n-manifold with boundary, and double it to obtain an n-manifold M together with a degree-one map f:M\to X. Stabilizing the normal bundle gives a well-defined normal invariant \eta(f)\in[X,G/TOP]. The Wall surgery machine packages the remaining obstruction into

	heta(\eta(f))\in L_n^{\langle1\rangle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]),

computed via the exact sequence 0\to S^{TOP}(X)\to[X,G/TOP]\xrightarrow{	heta}L_n^{\langle1\rangle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]). The 2-torsion lattice hypotheses ensure that the assembly map H_n(B\Gamma;\mathbb L_0)\to L_n^{\langle1\rangle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]) is trivial, so the obstruction lives in a torsion subgroup generated by low-degree characteristic classes. By adjusting \eta(f) within [X,G/TOP] (changing the normal data on finitely many cells) we can arrange 	heta(\eta(f))=0.

Once the obstruction vanishes, \eta(f) lifts to the structure set S^{TOP}(X). This lift corresponds to a closed manifold N and a simple homotopy equivalence N\to X inducing \pi_1(N)\cong\Gamma. Thus the chain of implications is: \omega(\Gamma)=0 \Rightarrow finite FH(\mathbb Q) complex \Rightarrow degree-one normal map \Rightarrow surgery obstruction in L_n^{\langle1\rangle}(\mathbb Z[\Gamma]) \Rightarrow (after vanishing) a genuine closed manifold with fundamental group \Gamma.

In short, finiteness gives a space of the right homotopy type, rational PD ensures it satisfies the Poincar'e duality hypotheses of surgery theory, and the vanishing of the L-group obstruction completes the passage to the manifold category.
